Dangling-reference repairs:
- "Pragmatism may be a happy harmonizer…": referring words "I wish now to add a word in further explanation of the claim I made at our last meeting, that" (first person plus outside-frame "our last meeting"). Repair: first-person cut. The trace starts at "pragmatism may be".
- "Men who are strongly of the fact-loving temperament{} are liable…": referring words "you may remember me to have said" (first person, outside-frame). Repair: first-person cut, mid-sentence, with `{}`.
- "But{, }the brand of pantheism offered…": referring words "as I said in my first lecture" (first person, outside-frame). Repair: first-person cut, mid-sentence, with joining ", ".
- "It is eminently a product of{} the rationalistic temper.": referring words "what I have ventured to call". Repair: first-person cut. These words only frame the author's naming.
- "In this real world of sweat and dirt{, }when a view of things is 'noble,'…": referring words "it seems to me that". Repair: first-person cut (author's stance).
- "What I{, }William James{, }said just now about the Absolute of transcendental idealism…": referring word "I". Repair: author name span from the `source:` line. It is the note's first "I", so the later "I", "me" and "my" in the note count as resolved, including "if I mistake not" and "to hear me say". "Said just now" points to statements earlier in this note.

Statements dropped:
- "Far be it from me to deny the majesty of this conception, or its capacity to yield religious comfort to a most respectable class of minds." The "me" carries the claim, so no cut works. The author name span cannot attach to "me", and no antecedent repairs it, so the statement is dropped. Its content is still carried by the kept sentence "First, I called it majestic and said it yielded religious comfort to a class of minds…".
- "But enough of this at present?" was dropped as a transition.
- "The justification of what I say must be postponed." was dropped as a forward hook.
- Not kept under the selection rule: "Like the sick lion in Esop's fable, all footprints lead into his den, but nulla vestigia retrorsum." It is an illustration.

Outside-frame references kept: none.

Generic "we"/"you" left unrepaired:
- "our contemporary imagination", "our world", "our human trials", "our minds and our experiences", "our lives", "we are the better for possessing it": these mean people in general.
- "we need only apply the pragmatic method": the author and reader working through the text together.
- "we may… treat the temporal", "we have a right ever and anon to take a moral holiday": the believers' generic "we" within the reported meaning.
- "as we are told he is": generic hearsay.
- "you" in "You cannot redescend…", "He gives you…", "so long as you get about…", "hearing you speak…", "some of you", "you will gladly admit", "you will allow", "you will say": addressed to the reader or audience.

Asides: none.
